# Torque, power and bus-timing budget (generated by `python -m analysis.report`; do not edit)

Generated 2026-11-06. Inputs: spec/kinematics.yaml (masses, lengths, servo rating, payload 0.25 kg); centres of mass from the generated CAD (hardware/cad). Nothing has been measured on hardware.

## 1. Static holding torque, arm stretched horizontally, payload at the TCP

Servo: stall 2.9 N*m; continuous = 40% of stall = 1.16 N*m (the spec's 1.0 A max continuous current corresponds to ~1.07 N*m on a linear torque-constant model, so the 40 % derating is the slightly optimistic one).

Counterbalance: zero-free-length spring, K = k*a*b = **1.309 N*m**, chosen to minimise the worst residual shoulder torque over all poses with shoulder in [-1.80, +0.80] rad (the mechanically reachable range), elbow and wrist over their full limits, payload 0 or 0.25 kg.

| joint | model | holding N*m (no CB) | with CB | % stall (no CB / CB) | margin vs continuous (no CB / CB) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shoulder_pitch | spec masses | 2.61 | 1.30 | 90 % / 45 % | x0.44 / x0.89 | intermittent only |
| elbow_pitch | spec masses | 1.30 | 1.30 | 45 % / 45 % | x0.89 / x0.89 | intermittent only |
| wrist_pitch | spec masses | 0.36 | 0.36 | 12 % / 12 % | x3.25 / x3.25 | OK continuous |
| shoulder_pitch | CAD masses | 2.49 | 1.18 | 86 % / 41 % | x0.47 / x0.98 | intermittent only |
| elbow_pitch | CAD masses | 1.29 | 1.29 | 45 % / 45 % | x0.90 / x0.90 | intermittent only |
| wrist_pitch | CAD masses | 0.39 | 0.39 | 13 % / 13 % | x2.99 / x2.99 | OK continuous |
| wrist_roll | CAD | 0.036 | - | 1.2 % | x33 | OK (payload on axis; gripper COM 21 mm off axis) |
| base_yaw | spec | 0 (vertical axis) | - | dynamic: I_zz 0.112 kg*m^2 x 15 rad/s^2 = 1.68 N*m (58 % stall) | x0.69 | peak only; limit yaw accel at full reach |
| gripper | - | squeeze force per jaw at stall 77 N, at continuous 31 N | - | needed for 0.25 kg (mu 0.5, SF 2.0): 4.9 N | x6.3 | OK; set a gripper current limit so it cannot crush objects |

Over the whole reachable pose set the worst residual shoulder torque WITH the counterbalance is **1.30 N*m** (spec masses) / 1.40 N*m (CAD masses); without it the worst is 2.61 N*m.

Counterbalance options (spec masses):

| choice | K (N*m) | residual at full reach, payload 0.25 kg | worst residual over all reachable poses |
|---|---|---|---|
| minimax over all poses (chosen) | 1.31 | 1.30 | 1.30 |
| balance stretched arm, no payload | 1.41 | 1.20 | 1.39 |
| balance stretched arm + half payload | 2.01 | 0.60 | 1.96 |

A larger K helps the common stretched poses but over-lifts when the elbow is folded back with the shoulder near horizontal; the minimax choice guarantees no reachable pose is worse than 1.30 N*m. K can be tuned later simply by moving pin B (K is proportional to b).

Largest payload that the servos can hold CONTINUOUSLY (40 % derating) at full horizontal reach: elbow **0.20 kg**, shoulder -0.05 kg without / **0.22 kg** with the counterbalance. The spec's 0.25 kg at full reach is therefore an intermittent (seconds) load for shoulder and elbow; for long data sessions keep heavy objects inside ~80 % reach or lower the rated payload.

Bearing load (yaw): overturning moment at full reach with payload = 2.61 N*m (spec masses) plus the shoulder bracket; carried by the 61812 thin-section bearing, not by the yaw servo.

## 2. Shoulder counterbalance spring

Geometry (from CAD): pulley A 40 mm above the shoulder axis on the bracket post; pin B 70 mm along the upper arm. Torque k*a*b*cos(q_shoulder) matches the cos-shaped gravity torque of the stretched arm at every shoulder angle (a zero-free-length spring), independent of yaw.

| quantity | reachable range | full spec range |
|---|---|---|
| rate k (N/mm) | 0.47 | 0.47 |
| initial tension Fi (N), = k x 0.8 x min AB | 11.22 | 11.22 |
| min distance AB (mm) | 30.00 | 30.00 |
| max distance AB (mm) | 102.60 | 109.07 |
| spring extension at max (mm) | 78.60 | 85.07 |
| max spring force (N) | 47.96 | 50.98 |

Realisation: cable from pin B over a ~10 mm pulley at A, down the post to an extension spring hooked at the post foot. Setting the cable length so the spring extension is AB - Fi/k makes the force exactly k*|AB| (equivalent zero free length) as long as the spring never goes slack. Choose a spring with rate ~0.47 N/mm, initial tension <= 14 N and >= 79 mm safe working extension (two springs in parallel at half rate are fine). No spring part number is given: pick from a catalogue and re-run this report with the real rate. The post and pin see up to the max spring force above.

## 3. 12 V servo-rail current budget

Linear current model I = 0.05 A idle (assumed) + (I_stall - idle) x tau/tau_stall.

| joint | static tau N*m (no CB) | I (A) no CB | I (A) with CB | stall I (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base_yaw | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.05 | 2.7 |
| shoulder_pitch | 2.61 | 2.43 | 1.24 | 2.7 |
| elbow_pitch | 1.30 | 1.24 | 1.24 | 2.7 |
| wrist_pitch | 0.39 | 0.41 | 0.41 | 2.7 |
| wrist_roll | 0.04 | 0.08 | 0.08 | 2.7 |
| gripper | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.05 | 2.7 |
| **sum static** | | **4.26** | **3.06** | **16.2** |

Board electronics (5 V + 3.3 V bucks, ~0.63 W at 85 %): 0.06 A at 12 V.

| case | 12 V current |
|---|---|
| static hold at full reach + payload, no CB | 4.3 A |
| static hold, with CB | 3.1 A |
| typical worst motion: static (no CB) + two joints accelerating at 80 % stall | 8.6 A |
| absolute worst: all six servos stalled at once | 16.3 A |

**PSU recommendation:** 12 V, **>= 12.5 A continuous (150 W)**, with a peak rating >= 16 A for >= 100 ms or a hard current limit that does not latch off. Rationale: the realistic worst motion is ~9 A; an all-servo stall (16 A) exceeds a 10 A brick, which would brown out the board. The spec PLAN's 12 V 10 A supply is the bare minimum and only works if the firmware current limits keep the sum below 10 A. Firmware/servo settings: per-servo protection current ~2.0 A, board OVERCURRENT fault at 12 A sustained > 20 ms on the INA240 reading. Input fuse 15 A slow-blow. Bulk capacitance on the servo rail (>= 1000 uF low-ESR) covers sub-millisecond stall edges only, not sustained stalls.

## 4. Servo bus timing (spec/protocol.md: 1 kHz loop, 1 Mbps, SYNC_WRITE 6 + 1 read per cycle)

### goal position only (2 B/servo)

| item | us |
|---|---|
| SYNC_WRITE (26 B) | 260 |
| READ request (8 B) | 80 |
| turnaround tx->rx | 2 |
| servo latency (assumed) | 100 |
| status reply (21 B) | 210 |
| turnaround rx->tx | 2 |
| CPU/DMA slack (assumed) | 30 |
| **total** | **684** (68% of the 1000 us cycle, margin 316 us) |

### position + time + speed (6 B/servo)

| item | us |
|---|---|
| SYNC_WRITE (50 B) | 500 |
| READ request (8 B) | 80 |
| turnaround tx->rx | 2 |
| servo latency (assumed) | 100 |
| status reply (21 B) | 210 |
| turnaround rx->tx | 2 |
| CPU/DMA slack (assumed) | 30 |
| **total** | **924** (92% of the 1000 us cycle, margin 76 us) |

8N1 framing (10 bits/byte). The read covers registers 0x38-0x46 (present position, speed, load, voltage, temperature, status, moving, present current) in one READ so the STATE frame gets pos/vel/current/temp from one transaction. Feetech packet layout as in the SCS/STS protocol (Dynamixel-1.0-like); register addresses are from the STS3215 memory table as commonly published and must be checked against the servo's datasheet. Servo response latency is ASSUMED (100 us); measure it on the first servo with a logic analyser. Verdict: fits in 1 ms with the 2-byte write; the 6-byte write is tight but fits; there is no room for a second read per cycle.
